plan:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (result stage — design only; NO experiment was run and no results are reported or claimed)

TITLE
Distributional similarity of forward-model-sampled trajectories vs ground-truth MD trajectories for all-atom tetrapeptides, evaluated on backbone torsions, sidechain torsions, and top TICA components.

===========================================================
1. QUESTION AND CLAIM UNDER TEST
===========================================================
Do sampled trajectories from the forward simulation model exhibit distributional similarity to ground-truth MD trajectories across key collective variables — backbone torsions, sidechain torsions, and top TICA components?

Fixed requirements (confirmed by researcher from setup): (i) all-atom MD of tetrapeptides; (ii) comparison CVs must include backbone torsions and sidechain torsions; (iii) top TICA components are in scope. Everything else (force field, trajectory lengths, TICA lag/components, sampling protocol) is stated below as DEFAULTS WITH RATIONALE, marked [CONTINGENT] — these are design choices to be replaced by paper-specific facts if/when the setup topics supply them, not established facts.

===========================================================
2. DATA SOURCE AND REFERENCE DEFINITION (two branches)
===========================================================
2.1 Ground-truth reference (two pre-specified branches, chosen by data availability, decided BEFORE any similarity computation):
  Branch R-A (preferred): held-out MD split. Reference = MD trajectories of the test peptides (or test segments of each peptide) that were NOT used to train the model and NOT used to fit TICA.
  Branch R-B (fallback): full released MD set used as reference, with an explicit leakage caveat: metrics then quantify consistency with the data the model may have seen; this weakens the claim from "generalization" to "distribution match on observed data." Any result under R-B must be labeled as such in reporting.
  [CONTINGENT] Source of trajectories: released ground-truth MD from the NeurIPS 2024 paper (ID 93022); if a test split exists, R-A; else R-B.

2.2 Model-sampled set:
  - Sampled trajectories produced by the paper's forward simulation model, using the paper's sampling protocol [CONTINGENT: number of independent rollouts per initial state, rollout length, integration/model step]. Default if unspecified: run enough independent rollouts to produce ≥ 5× the number of frames in the reference for each peptide (rationale: model samples are cheap; oversampling lets us verify metric convergence rather than being limited by sample count).
  - Initialization: seed sampled rollouts from the same initial states as held-out MD segments where available; if the model's protocol initializes elsewhere (e.g., its own initial distribution), record this as a deviation and run a sensitivity arm (Section 8).

2.3 Atom mapping / preprocessing branch (mandatory preprocessing check before any CV extraction):
  Step P1: assert identical residue count, residue names, and atom names between a reference frame and a sampled frame (MDTopology comparison). If identical → direct torsion extraction.
  Step P2 (fallback if ordering/renumbering differs): canonical renumbering by residue sequence and standard atom names; verify by re-checking torsion ranges on a few frames (e.g., φ/ψ values of a reference frame must be reproducible after renumbering within 1°).
  Step P3 (fallback if coordinates are rotated/translated inconsistently): torsions are internal coordinates and invariant to rigid-body motion, so no alignment is needed for torsions; alignment is only needed if any Cartesian CVs were added (out of scope here). Record which branch (P1/P2) each dataset required; if P2 fails validation, that peptide's sampled data is excluded and reported as a preprocessing failure, not as dissimilarity.

===========================================================
3. COLLECTIVE VARIABLES (computed identically for both sets, same topology selection)
===========================================================
3.1 Backbone torsions:
  - Per residue i (excluding terminal residues' undefined angles): φ_i = C(i-1)–N(i)–Cα(i)–C(i); ψ_i = N(i)–Cα(i)–C(i)–N(i+1); ω_i = Cα(i)–C(i)–N(i+1)–Cα(i+1) [ω included by default since isomerization is a real CV; marked CONTINGENT — drop if the paper's protocol excludes it]. Terminal residues contribute the defined subset (ψ of residue 1, φ of residue N).
  - For a generic tetrapeptide: up to 3 φ, 3 ψ, 3 ω → ~6–9 backbone CVs per peptide.

3.2 Sidechain torsions:
  - χ angles per residue, computed from standard tetrahedral definitions (χ1 for all non-Gly/Ala residues; χ2..χn for longer sidechains). For glycine/alanine (no χ1), the residue contributes no sidechain CVs and is recorded as such. Exact peptide sequences are [CONTINGENT] (unknown from workspace); the design is sequence-agnostic.

3.3 TICA components:
  - Featurization for TICA: all torsions from 3.1 and 3.2, transformed to circular features (sin/cos pairs per torsion) to respect periodicity [default; rationale: raw linear torsions create artificial discontinuities at ±π that corrupt TICA eigenmodes].
  - Fitting: TICA is fit ONCE on reference MD frames only (Branch R-A: held-out reference; if the reference set is small, fit on training MD and treat held-out MD purely as evaluation — this is the cleaner variant and is the default if a training split exists). Freeze the TICA model (means, whitening, eigenvectors).
  - Hyperparameters [CONTINGENT, defaults with rationale]: lag time τ = a short multiple of the MD torsion autocorrelation time; default τ = 10 × MD frame spacing or the paper's stated value, whichever is available; number of components = top 10 (report top 4 separately, since the question says "top TICA components"); kinetic map scaling.
  - Projection: both reference and sampled trajectories are projected through the frozen model. Sampled data NEVER enters fitting.

  Implied timescale sanity check (feasibility/validity control): verify the chosen τ lies on the approximate plateau of the implied timescales computed from the reference; if not, adjust τ once, then freeze — no re-tuning after seeing model-sample results.

===========================================================
4. SIMILARITY METRICS (full specification)
===========================================================
All metrics computed per peptide (primary) and pooled across peptides (secondary, explicitly labeled as such).

4.1 1D torsion distributions (backbone + sidechain):
  - Estimator: circular histogram with B = 72 bins (5° resolution) with periodic wrapping; sensitivity check at B = 36 and B = 144 to confirm metric stability.
  - Metric: Jensen–Shannon distance (JSD, base-2 log, bounded [0,1]) between reference and sampled histograms, per torsion. Secondary descriptive: circular KL (symmetrized) for reference only if JSD trends need decomposition.
  - Significance: permutation test per torsion — pool reference and sampled frames, randomly reassign group labels (preserving sample sizes) 1,000 times, recompute JSD, p-value = fraction of permuted JSD ≥ observed. Multiple-testing: Benjamini–Hochberg FDR 0.05 across all torsions within a peptide.
  - Circular two-sample test as a second opinion: Watson U-test per torsion (circular analog of the two-sample test); report agreement between the two test families as a robustness check.

4.2 2D Ramachandran / free-energy overlap:
  - Per residue: joint P(φ,ψ) on a 36×36 grid (10° bins) with periodic wrap on both axes; free energy F = −k_BT ln P with per-bin counts floored at a pseudocount (Laplace +1) to avoid −ln 0.
  - Metric: JSD between the 2D histograms; plus a basin-overlap statistic: identify the 2–4 highest-probability basins in the reference (connected high-density regions), and report (a) fraction of sampled probability mass falling in reference basins, (b) whether any reference basin contains < 1% of sampled mass (a "missing mode" flag). Free-energy RMSE in units of k_BT over bins where both distributions have support ≥ some floor.
  - k_BT uses the simulation temperature of the MD setup [CONTINGENT; default 300 K only for descriptive free energies — note JSD itself is temperature-free, so the decision rule never depends on this default].

4.3 TICA-space overlap:
  - Multivariate two-sample metrics on the projected coordinates (top 10 TICA components):
    (a) Energy distance (E-statistic) between reference and sampled point clouds, with permutation p-value (1,000 permutations).
    (b) Maximum mean discrepancy (MMD², unbiased estimator) with RBF kernel; bandwidth = median heuristic computed on reference only.
    (c) k-NN two-sample classifier (k = 5): train on half of each set, evaluate AUC on the other half; AUC ≈ 0.5 ⇒ indistinguishable, AUC → 1 ⇒ distinguishable. Repeated with 20 random splits; report mean AUC and CI.
  - Per-component 1D TICA histograms: JSD per component (top 4 individually reported), as a human-readable decomposition.
  - Metastable-basin populations: assign frames to the top 2–4 TICA microstates (k-means on reference-projected data, frozen); compare state populations via a two-proportion z-test / chi-square, and total variation distance between state-population vectors. This checks that the model reproduces slow-mode weights, not just marginals.

4.4 Temporal fidelity (secondary, clearly separated from the distributional question):
  - The question is distributional, so temporal accuracy is NOT part of the decision rule; however, report autocorrelation functions of the top TICA components and of torsions in both sets, plus the implied-timescale comparison, as descriptive context. A distributionally-perfect but dynamically-wrong model must be labeled as such.

===========================================================
5. CONTROLS (full specification)
===========================================================
5.1 Positive control (noise floor): split the reference MD into two disjoint halves (by trajectory or by contiguous time blocks — time blocks preferred to preserve independence; per-trajectory split if trajectories are independent). Compute ALL metrics of Section 4 between the two halves. This is the finite-sampling floor: any real comparison cannot be expected to beat it. If a metric between model and reference is at or below the positive-control value, that dimension is "at noise floor" (best achievable).

5.2 Negative baselines (must be clearly distinguishable from reference, else the metric battery lacks power):
  N1 — Surrogate/shuffle baseline: reference frames shuffled in time (destroys temporal structure, preserves exact marginals). Expected outcome: passes 1D marginal metrics (by construction), fails TICA-space metrics and temporal checks — this validates that TICA metrics carry information beyond marginals.
  N2 — Time-reversed reference: same marginal structure, reversed dynamics; expected to fail TICA/metastable checks.
  N3 — Degenerate sampler: sample torsions i.i.d. from the reference marginals per torsion (breaks joint correlation structure), build synthetic trajectories; expected to pass per-torsion 1D JSD but fail 2D Ramachandran and TICA-space metrics — validates that 2D/multivariate metrics detect correlation errors.
  N4 — (if implementable) wrong-physics baseline, e.g., MD at elevated temperature or a coarse prior of the model; expected to fail broadly. [CONTINGENT on availability of any alternative generator; omit if not obtainable and state so.]

5.3 Sample-size sensitivity: repeat the primary metrics at 1×, 2×, 5× sampled-frame counts; report convergence curves. If metrics are still drifting at 5×, report the minimum sample size at which the per-peptide decision stabilizes.

5.4 TICA leakage control: recompute the headline TICA metrics with a TICA model fit on a different random subset of reference frames; the reference-vs-model comparison must not change qualitatively (frozen-model robustness).

===========================================================
6. ANALYSIS PLAN — PRE-SPECIFIED DECISION RULES
===========================================================
Primary decision rule (relative, per peptide):
  D1 (torsions): median per-torsion JSD over all backbone+sidechain torsions of the peptide ≤ median positive-control JSD + 2 robust SEs (bootstrap), AND the number of torsions failing the FDR-corrected permutation test is not significantly greater than the number failing in the positive control (Fisher exact test on fail counts, α = 0.05).
  D2 (Ramachandran): per-residue 2D JSD ≤ positive-control 2D JSD + 2 robust SEs, AND zero reference basins flagged "missing mode" (Section 4.2) beyond those flagged in the positive control.
  D3 (TICA space): energy distance and MMD² permutation p-values ≥ 0.05 (cannot reject H0: same distribution) OR k-NN AUC within the positive-control AUC ± its bootstrap CI; total-variation distance of TICA microstate populations ≤ positive control + 2 robust SEs.
  Overall per-peptide verdict: "similar at noise floor" iff D1 ∧ D2 ∧ D3; "partially similar" if 2 of 3 pass; "dissimilar" otherwise. Failures must be localized (which torsions / which TICA components / which basins).

Secondary descriptive summaries (absolute, non-decisional): pooled median JSD per CV family; pooled k-NN AUC; pooled energy distance; free-energy RMSE in k_BT; with bootstrap 95% CIs. These are reported for context only and cannot flip the primary verdict.

Uncertainty quantification: ALL CIs are bootstrap over independent trajectories (resample whole trajectories with replacement, ≥ 1,000 bootstrap replicates), never over frames, because frames within a trajectory are autocorrelated. For peptide-level population claims, also report the across-peptide distribution (median, IQR) of each metric and a paired comparison model-vs-positive-control across peptides (Wilcoxon signed-rank over peptides, α = 0.05) to say whether the model is systematically worse than the noise floor.

Power/sanity pre-check before unblinding: confirm the negative controls are significantly separated from the positive control on every metric (if not, the metric has no discriminative power and the design's decision rule is invalid — report this as a design failure, not as model similarity).

Reporting template: per peptide × per CV family table of {metric value, positive control, negative controls, bootstrap CI, verdict}; convergence curves; TICA implied timescales; preprocessing branch used.

===========================================================
7. FEASIBILITY (if the experiment were to be run — it has NOT been)
===========================================================
- Software: Python with numpy/scipy/scikit-learn, mdtraj or MDAnalysis for torsion extraction from trajectories, deeptime (or MSMBuilder/pyEMMA equivalent) for TICA. None are preinstalled in this environment (verified: numpy, scipy, sklearn, mdtraj, mdanalysis, deeptime all absent); a real run would require installing these — feasible on CPU (TICA on tetrapeptide torsion features is low-dimensional and cheap; the heavy step is running the generative model if sampled trajectories are not released).
- Compute: no GPU strictly required for analysis; GPU needed only if the forward model must be re-run to generate samples. Tetrapeptide scale (few sequences, torsion-only features) keeps TICA and metric computation to minutes on a single CPU core. Estimated total analyst time: data acquisition/verification dominates.
- Risks: (a) sampled trajectories not released → must re-run model (needs checkpoint + code, GPU); (b) no held-out split (→ Branch R-B with leakage caveat); (c) atom-mapping failures (→ Section 2.3 exclusion protocol); (d) reference MD too short for stable TICA at the default lag (→ reduce lag to the plateau onset, fewer components, and report the timescale-resolution limitation).

===========================================================
8. PRE-SPECIFIED CONTINGENCY / SENSITIVITY ARMS
===========================================================
S1: If sampled trajectories are released rather than generated by us — skip 2.2 generation, run everything else identically; report release provenance.
S2: If the paper prescribes its own TICA procedure — run it as an alternative arm (Arm B) alongside the primary frozen-reference-only TICA (Arm A); headline results from Arm A, Arm B reported for comparability.
S3: If reference is the full MD set (R-B) — all verdicts labeled "leakage-possible"; additionally report the held-out-by-time-block analysis (train blocks vs test blocks of the same trajectories) as a partial mitigation.
S4: If the model initializes from states different from MD test starts — add an initialization-matched sub-analysis restricted to shared initial states, if any exist.
S5: If any peptide fails preprocessing validation (P2), it is excluded from verdicts and listed; the overall claim then reads "for N of M peptides."

===========================================================
9. STATEMENT
===========================================================
No experiment was run. No data was generated, no metrics were computed, and no results exist. Everything above is a prospective design; all setup specifics beyond the three fixed requirements are defaults/contingencies to be confirmed against the paper's actual setup (topics setup_2 / setup_13 / setup_14) before execution.
